title: IP Addresses and Network Paths
summary: Understand IPv4 addresses, gateways, and possible path failures using a closed simulation.
objectives: Explain that an IP address identifies a device or interface on a network.
Identify possible failure points in a simulated device-to-server path.

vocab.def: A network address used to identify a device or interface.
A device or service that connects a local network to another network.
A common address format written as four numbers separated by dots.

sections.heading: Addresses identify interfaces
sections.body: An IPv4 address is commonly written as four numbers separated by dots. In a network model, the address helps identify where information should go; it does not describe every detail about the device.

sections.heading: Follow the path
sections.body: A simplified path is device interface, switch, gateway, network, and server interface. A broken link, wrong address, unavailable gateway, or server issue can affect the result.

sections.heading: Closed and authorized practice
sections.body: Use only synthetic addresses and a classroom simulator. Do not scan real networks, change external configurations, or test systems without authorization. Subnet mathematics can be introduced later.

practice.prompt: A device has an address but cannot reach a server. Name two path points to inspect in a simulation and explain why.

quiz.question: What is an IP address used for?
options: Identify a device or interface on a network
quiz.answer: Identify a device or interface on a network

lab.objective: Diagnose a synthetic IP and gateway path using provided observations.

futureCompetencyCandidates: identify simulated network path failure points
